findings.evidence: grep: `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Representation/Basic.lean:36:abbrev QuiverRep (k : Type u) (Q : Type v) [Field k] [Quiver Q] := Paths Q ⥤ ModuleCat k`, whose module doc says "The equivalence with modules over the path algebra is planned for separate development"; no occurrence of `QuiverRep` or `dimVector` in ModuleDecomposition.lean.
findings.fix: Add an implementation-notes paragraph stating plainly that only the underlying data and its functoriality are proved here and that no `TauCeti.QuiverRep` object/functor is assembled (noting the `CommSemiring k` vs `Field k` gap), and cross-reference `TauCeti.QuiverRep` and `TauCeti.dimVector`; drop or qualify "really is a representation of `Q`".
findings.issue: The header ("A module over a path algebra is a representation of the quiver") and the docstrings at lines 93 ("the value at `v` of the representation of `Q` attached to `M`"), 132 ("the structure maps of the representation of `Q` attached to `M`") and 156 ("this says that `v ↦ eᵥ M` really is a representation of `Q`") present a representation as existing, but no `TauCeti.QuiverRep k Q` (`abbrev QuiverRep ... := Paths Q ⥤ ModuleCat k`, Representation/Basic.lean:36) is built and that type is never named anywhere in the file. Same for line 223's "read off the dimension vector", where `TauCeti.dimVector` already exists (Representation/DimensionVector.lean:44).

findings.evidence: Module.lean:253 `theorem finrank_eq_sum_finrank_smulRange [Module.Finite S M]`; ModuleDecomposition.lean:220 `[Module.Finite k M]`.
findings.fix: State the hypothesis in both docstrings, e.g. "for a module finite-dimensional over `S` (resp. `k`), the dimensions of the pieces add up to the dimension of the module".
findings.issue: "over a field the dimensions of the pieces add up to the dimension of the module" promises more than the statement, which assumes `[Module.Finite S M]`; without it the claim is false (an infinite-dimensional piece gives `finrank = 0` on the left while other pieces contribute on the right). Same omission in `finrank_eq_sum_finrank_vertexComponent` (ModuleDecomposition.lean:222) and in the module-doc bullets at Module.lean:53 and ModuleDecomposition.lean:48.

findings.evidence: Module.lean:40 is the sole Main-definitions bullet; Module.lean:223 `noncomputable def smulRangeDirectSumEquiv`; Module.lean:52 references `TauCeti.coe_smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_symm_apply`.
findings.fix: Add a bullet: `TauCeti.smulRangeDirectSumEquiv`: the `S`-linear isomorphism `⨁ᵢ eᵢ M ≃ M`.
findings.issue: "## Main definitions" lists only `smulRange`, omitting `smulRangeDirectSumEquiv` (line 223), the file's other public definition — yet "Main results" cites `coe_smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_symm_apply`, so the header names a lemma about an object it never introduces.

summary: Docstrings are mostly accurate and the roadmap quotations check out, but the new quiver file's documentation speaks throughout of "the representation of Q attached to M" while never constructing or even mentioning the in-repo `TauCeti.QuiverRep`, and both `finrank` docstrings drop the finiteness hypothesis their statements require.
